title: Grammar in Context
tagline: Hear the difference. Say exactly what you mean.
description: Build precision in English through everyday decisions, conversations, and small surprises. Practice the grammar that changes timing, certainty, emphasis, and perspective.

chapters.title: Time and Perspective
chapters.description: Follow routines, recent changes, unfinished efforts, and future plans as time shifts around them.

sentences.text: I've known Maya for years, but we've only worked together since January.
sentences.hint: A long friendship became a professional connection only recently.

sentences.text: When I reached the station, the last train had already left.
sentences.hint: I arrived too late to catch the final service.

sentences.text: The cafe usually closes at six, but it's staying open later this week.
sentences.hint: Opening hours are temporarily different from the normal schedule.

sentences.text: I've been trying to reach you all morning; did you leave your phone at home?
sentences.hint: Several unsuccessful calls make me wonder where your phone is.

sentences.text: We'd been walking for an hour when we realized we were heading in the wrong direction.
sentences.hint: A long walk continued before we noticed our navigation mistake.

sentences.text: By the time the guests arrive, we'll have finished setting the table.
sentences.hint: Dinner preparations should be complete before anyone gets here.

sentences.text: I was going to complain, but the manager offered a refund before I said anything.
sentences.hint: An unexpected solution made my planned objection unnecessary.

sentences.text: This time tomorrow, I'll be sitting on a train instead of answering emails.
sentences.hint: I expect to be traveling during tomorrow's usual work hours.

sentences.text: I didn't realize how tired I was until I'd sat down.
sentences.hint: Resting made me notice how little energy I had.

sentences.text: We're meeting the landlord tomorrow about the leak that's been getting worse.
sentences.hint: A scheduled discussion will address an increasingly serious maintenance problem.

chapters.title: Certainty, Permission, and Responsibility
chapters.description: Weigh possibilities, make requests, explain obligations, and look back on choices.

sentences.text: You don't have to stay until the end if you've got an early start tomorrow.
sentences.hint: Leaving early is acceptable with a busy morning ahead.

sentences.text: You must have been relieved when they finally found your suitcase.
sentences.hint: I'm almost certain recovering your luggage eased your worry.

sentences.text: We might need another pair of hands if the delivery arrives before lunch.
sentences.hint: An early shipment could leave us short of help.

sentences.text: I should have checked the address instead of assuming I knew the way.
sentences.hint: I regret trusting my memory rather than confirming the location.

sentences.text: Visitors must sign in at reception, even if they're only staying for a few minutes.
sentences.hint: Brief visits still require registration at the front desk.

sentences.text: That can't be Leo at the door; he's still on his flight.
sentences.hint: His current journey makes his presence here impossible.

sentences.text: Could you keep an eye on my bag while I buy the tickets?
sentences.hint: I'm politely asking you to watch my belongings briefly.

sentences.text: You needn't have brought any food; the hosts had already arranged everything.
sentences.hint: Your contribution was unnecessary because the meal was covered.

sentences.text: The council ought to explain why the repairs are taking so long.
sentences.hint: Residents deserve an account of the delay in maintenance.

sentences.text: We were able to save most of the photos, although the laptop never worked again.
sentences.hint: We successfully recovered the images despite losing the computer.

chapters.title: Conditions and Consequences
chapters.description: Connect practical arrangements, imagined alternatives, and past decisions with their consequences.

sentences.text: If you send me the draft tonight, I'll read it before our meeting.
sentences.hint: Receiving your work this evening will allow an advance review.

sentences.text: If I lived closer to the office, I'd cycle instead of taking the bus.
sentences.hint: The distance from my home prevents a different commute.

sentences.text: If we'd booked the earlier train, we wouldn't have missed the opening speech.
sentences.hint: A different travel choice would have prevented our late arrival.

sentences.text: Unless the weather improves, we'll move the picnic into the community hall.
sentences.hint: The gathering will be indoors if conditions remain poor.

sentences.text: You can borrow my camera as long as you return it before Friday.
sentences.hint: Permission depends on bringing the equipment back by a deadline.

sentences.text: If I hadn't taken that course, I wouldn't be doing this job now.
sentences.hint: A past learning decision made my current career possible.

sentences.text: Even if the restaurant is full, we can get something from the market.
sentences.hint: Unavailable tables won't stop us from finding a meal.

sentences.text: Take a spare key in case the front door locks behind you.
sentences.hint: Prepare now to avoid being accidentally shut outside.

sentences.text: Had I known the road was closed, I'd have taken the route by the river.
sentences.hint: Missing information prevented me from choosing a different road.

sentences.text: Provided that everyone agrees, we can postpone the vote until next week.
sentences.hint: Delaying the decision requires the whole group's approval.

chapters.title: Actions in the Spotlight
chapters.description: Focus on affected people, ongoing work, official procedures, and completed results.

sentences.text: The road is being resurfaced, so buses are using the next street.
sentences.hint: Current repairs mean public transport has temporarily been rerouted.

sentences.text: All successful applicants will be invited to a short interview next month.
sentences.hint: Selected candidates can expect a brief conversation in the coming weeks.

sentences.text: My bike was stolen while I was picking up a parcel.
sentences.hint: Someone took my bicycle during a brief collection errand.

sentences.text: The results haven't been published yet, despite several requests for an update.
sentences.hint: Repeated inquiries have not led to the findings becoming available.

sentences.text: By the time we arrived, the damaged windows had already been replaced.
sentences.hint: The broken glass was dealt with before we got there.

sentences.text: Hot drinks aren't allowed near the computers, even during evening classes.
sentences.hint: The beverage restriction applies to late lessons too.

sentences.text: The original design was changed after concerns were raised about wheelchair access.
sentences.hint: Accessibility objections led to revisions in the initial plan.

sentences.text: I was given the wrong room number, which explains why nobody recognized me.
sentences.hint: Incorrect directions sent me into a gathering of strangers.

sentences.text: This old theater is said to be haunted, although I've never heard anything unusual.
sentences.hint: Local ghost stories don't match my own experience here.

sentences.text: The final payment must be received before the keys can be handed over.
sentences.hint: Access to the property depends on settling the remaining balance.

chapters.title: Passing the Message On
chapters.description: Share conversations, relay questions, and report promises, warnings, and admissions.

sentences.text: Amir said he'd call as soon as he knew whether the offer was genuine.
sentences.hint: He planned to contact me after checking the proposal's authenticity.

sentences.text: She told me she had never felt so nervous before an interview.
sentences.hint: She described unusually intense anxiety ahead of a hiring conversation.

sentences.text: The receptionist asked whether we'd made a reservation or were just visiting.
sentences.hint: The person at the desk wanted to clarify our booking status.

sentences.text: Our coach reminded us not to leave our water bottles on the bus.
sentences.hint: We were prompted to take our drinks when getting off.

sentences.text: I asked the mechanic how long the repair would take.
sentences.hint: I wanted an estimate of when the vehicle would be ready.

sentences.text: They warned us that the path could become slippery after rain.
sentences.hint: We were advised about a possible walking hazard in wet conditions.

sentences.text: Lena admitted that she'd forgotten to attach the document to her email.
sentences.hint: She acknowledged accidentally sending a message without the required file.

sentences.text: He denied taking the charger, but offered to help us look for it.
sentences.hint: He rejected responsibility while volunteering to join the search.

sentences.text: The landlord promised to deal with the heating problem before the weekend.
sentences.hint: The property owner committed to fixing the warmth issue soon.

sentences.text: When I asked why she was leaving, she said she needed a fresh start.
sentences.hint: Her explanation for departing was a desire to begin again.

chapters.title: Details That Matter
chapters.description: Identify people and places, add background, and connect events with useful extra detail.

sentences.text: The neighbor who helped me move has just opened a bakery.
sentences.hint: Someone from nearby who assisted with my relocation now sells bread.

sentences.text: I finally found the receipt that I'd been looking for all afternoon.
sentences.hint: A lengthy search ended with the missing proof of purchase.

sentences.text: Our new manager, whose office is next to mine, used to work abroad.
sentences.hint: My nearby colleague in charge has overseas professional experience.

sentences.text: The village where my grandparents met has hardly changed in fifty years.
sentences.hint: The setting of a family romance remains much as it was.

sentences.text: We stayed until the final song, which turned out to be the best part of the concert.
sentences.hint: Waiting for the ending rewarded us with the performance's highlight.

sentences.text: Anyone who needs a quieter workspace can use the room upstairs.
sentences.hint: People seeking fewer distractions have an alternative area available.

sentences.text: The people we rented the flat from were happy to extend our stay.
sentences.hint: Our accommodation hosts readily agreed to a longer visit.

sentences.text: There's a point at which saving time starts to cost too much money.
sentences.hint: Beyond a certain limit, convenience becomes unreasonably expensive.

sentences.text: The book you recommended makes a complicated subject surprisingly easy to follow.
sentences.hint: Your reading suggestion helped me understand something difficult.

sentences.text: I spoke to a woman whose luggage had been sent to a different airport.
sentences.hint: A fellow traveler described her bags reaching the wrong destination.

chapters.title: Making Fair Comparisons
chapters.description: Compare experiences, costs, changing situations, and the trade-offs behind everyday decisions.

sentences.text: The new apartment is slightly smaller than our old one, but it gets far more light.
sentences.hint: We traded a little space for a much brighter home.

sentences.text: This route takes twice as long on foot, though the walk is much more pleasant.
sentences.hint: The nicer walking option requires double the time.

sentences.text: The longer we waited for an explanation, the less confident we felt.
sentences.hint: Our trust declined as the unanswered delay continued.

sentences.text: The second proposal isn't nearly as risky as the first one.
sentences.hint: The later suggestion involves considerably less danger.

sentences.text: Of all the places we visited, the little museum by the harbor surprised me most.
sentences.hint: A modest waterfront attraction exceeded my expectations more than anywhere else.

sentences.text: It's becoming harder and harder to find a quiet place to study.
sentences.hint: Locating a peaceful learning spot is increasingly difficult.

sentences.text: I find it less tiring to work four longer days than five shorter ones.
sentences.hint: A shorter working week leaves me with more energy.

sentences.text: The repairs cost a great deal more than we'd expected.
sentences.hint: Fixing the damage was much pricier than our estimate.

sentences.text: Her latest talk was just as engaging as the one she gave last year.
sentences.hint: Both presentations held my attention equally well.

sentences.text: No other candidate had as much practical experience as Daniel.
sentences.hint: He led the applicant group in hands-on knowledge.

chapters.title: Connecting the Bigger Picture
chapters.description: Link reasons, results, purposes, and contrasting viewpoints into connected thoughts.

sentences.text: Although the tickets were expensive, we felt the experience was worth it.
sentences.hint: The high admission price didn't outweigh our enjoyment.

sentences.text: The library has extended its opening hours so that students can study after work.
sentences.hint: Later access is intended to support learners with daytime jobs.

sentences.text: I'd like to join you; however, I've already promised to help my sister move.
sentences.hint: A prior family commitment prevents me from accepting your invitation.

sentences.text: The instructions were unclear, which is why several people filled in the wrong section.
sentences.hint: Confusing guidance caused multiple mistakes on the form.

sentences.text: Despite having no formal training, she built a successful career as a photographer.
sentences.hint: She achieved professional success without studying the craft officially.

sentences.text: We decided to stay another night because the storm had made the roads unsafe.
sentences.hint: Dangerous travel conditions persuaded us to delay our departure.

sentences.text: The new system saves time; on the other hand, it takes a while to learn.
sentences.hint: Greater efficiency comes with an initial learning effort.

sentences.text: The workshop improved my skills and, more importantly, introduced me to people I could work with.
sentences.hint: Training brought useful knowledge and even more valuable professional connections.

sentences.text: I agreed with his main point, whereas the rest of the group rejected it completely.
sentences.hint: My support contrasted sharply with everyone else's opposition.

sentences.text: We left early in order to avoid the queues at the entrance.
sentences.hint: An earlier departure was intended to reduce waiting.

chapters.title: Questions with an Intention
chapters.description: Ask tactfully, check assumptions, challenge decisions, and seek more precise explanations.

sentences.text: Would you mind telling me why the deadline has been brought forward?
sentences.hint: I'm politely requesting the reason for an earlier due date.

sentences.text: What would it take to persuade you to stay for another year?
sentences.hint: Which changes might convince you to remain longer?

sentences.text: You haven't already sent the invitation, have you?
sentences.hint: I'm checking my assumption that the invite hasn't gone out.

sentences.text: How come nobody mentioned the extra charge when we made the booking?
sentences.hint: I'm surprised a further fee wasn't disclosed earlier.

sentences.text: Could you explain how this option differs from the one we discussed yesterday?
sentences.hint: I want clarification of the distinction between two alternatives.

sentences.text: Who was it that first suggested turning the empty shop into a library?
sentences.hint: I'm trying to identify the originator of a community idea.

sentences.text: Is there any reason we can't deal with the simpler tasks first?
sentences.hint: I'm tactfully proposing that we begin with easier work.

sentences.text: Wouldn't it make more sense to ask the team before changing the schedule?
sentences.hint: I believe consultation should come ahead of timetable adjustments.

sentences.text: Do you happen to know if the last bus stops outside the hospital?
sentences.hint: I'm gently seeking information about an evening transport connection.

sentences.text: Why should we accept a solution that creates more problems than it solves?
sentences.hint: I'm challenging the value of an apparently counterproductive proposal.

chapters.title: Imagining Different Choices
chapters.description: Express preferences, revisit regrets, and picture how life could be different.

sentences.text: I'd rather take a smaller room than share a wall with the elevator.
sentences.hint: For me, avoiding machinery noise matters more than extra space.

sentences.text: If only we'd left earlier, we could have explored the old town.
sentences.hint: I regret a late departure that prevented some sightseeing.

sentences.text: I wish I could remember the name of the person who recommended this place.
sentences.hint: I'm frustrated that I can't recall who suggested coming here.

sentences.text: Suppose your company offered you a year abroad; would you accept?
sentences.hint: Consider your response to a hypothetical temporary overseas assignment.

sentences.text: It's time we stopped treating every minor delay as an emergency.
sentences.hint: We should already be reacting more calmly to small setbacks.

sentences.text: Without your advice, I'd probably still be waiting for the perfect opportunity.
sentences.hint: Your guidance helped me act instead of endlessly putting things off.

sentences.text: I'd have preferred to discuss the problem in person rather than over the phone.
sentences.hint: Looking back, a face-to-face conversation would have suited me better.

sentences.text: Imagine waking up tomorrow with a whole week free and no appointments to keep.
sentences.hint: Picture suddenly having several days entirely to yourself.

sentences.text: You talk as if moving abroad would solve every problem.
sentences.hint: I'm questioning your belief that relocating could fix everything.

sentences.text: If you could change one decision from last year, which would you choose?
sentences.hint: Consider a single past choice you'd like to make differently.
